noi_dung:
Introduction to the Life Story

(Jàtaka)

(...) The Jataka (Buddha's Previous Birth Stories) is the most voluminous series in the Pali Canon. This set includes 6 large volumes, divided into 22 chapters, arranged in increasing order of the number of verses in the following chapters.

Each previous story consists of 3 parts:

1) Present story: is the part of dependent origination, an event related to Buddha, Dharma, Sangha or the masses has become the topic of discussion of the Sangha at the Dharma hall. On that occasion, the Buddha told a story from the past at the request of these people.

The previous stories were gradually gathered in the North India region, that is, the Central Plains (Madhyadesa) region of ancient India. First of all, the story only includes verses, so the verses are considered the most ancient part of this story. Some verses were inspired by the Buddha himself and others were created later by monks. Each story usually begins with a row of verses.

In volumes I and II, each volume includes 150 stories, with one or two verses. But from volume III onwards, the number of verses gradually increases. Therefore, the story is longer, until volume VI is the Great Product, which only includes 10 stories with hundreds of verses in each story, and ends at number 547 - Vessantara's predecessor is famous for thousands of verses. Thus, the entire Jataka Tales has about nearly 5,000 verses.

Most current stories are real events that happened during Buddha's time or several hundred years later. Therefore, this collection of stories is considered an invaluable source of information for historians and archaeologists who want to understand the political, social, religious, cultural context or customs of ancient India.

Many scholars and scholars have confirmed that this set of previous stories opened a new era in Buddhist literature to spread the Dharma widely to all classes of people, from intellectuals to ordinary people. Because this is a literary treasure that harmoniously combines Buddha's teachings according to the tradition of scholarly scriptures with the rich and diverse tradition of human fairy tales that were very popular in ancient India. Thanks to that, this series of stories has become an endless source of inspiration for the creative activities of poetry, musicals, painting, sculpture..., from ancient times to the present. (...)

(Excerpt from the monthly magazine Giac Ngo, No. 58, January 2001)

noi_dung:
The Story of the Wolf-headed Woman

Minor Nikaya - The Tale of Hungry Ghosts

The Master told this story while staying at Sàvatthì.

Once upon a time in Bebares (Ba la Nai), there was a woman who lived thanks to her beauty. At that time, her hair was very long, black, smooth, soft and shiny, curled up very beautifully. Her braids are tied into two fists, each time they hang down to her waist. At that time, some jealous women discussed and after bribing her maid, sent her a medicine that would destroy her hair. At that time, the maid mixed the medicine into bath powder and gave it to her master when he went to bathe in the Ganges River. She used the mixed medicine to thoroughly soak her hair to the roots and jumped into the water. As soon as she immersed herself in the water, her hair immediately fell out by the roots, clean and smooth, and her head resembled a bitter melon.

After that, looking as ugly as a pigeon with all its feathers plucked out, she was ashamed and did not dare to enter the city anymore, so she had to cover her head and live outside the city. When the shame was over and she knew how to press sesame seeds, she made a living selling oil and strong wine.

One day, when three drunk men fell asleep, she stole all their clothes that were hanging there. Then one day, she saw a Saint monk begging for alms. After inviting him in, she offered a cake made of chestnuts mixed with sesame oil. Out of compassion for her, he accepted the bread and ate it.

She stood there with a joyful heart, covering him with a parasol. The elder was moved, said words of joy and merit and left.

Later she passed away, thanks to her good karma, she was reborn in the middle of an ocean alone in a golden castle, her hair was restored as she wished. But because she stole the men's clothes, now she must be naked. She kept reincarnating in that golden castle and had to live naked for a lifetime there.

Later, the World-Honored One came to earth, while he was staying in Sàvatthì, one hundred merchants whose houses were there boarded a boat to the land of Suvanbhùmi (Golden Land). Their boat was caught in a storm and drifted to the other shore. At that moment, the female demon and the castle appeared before them. When the leader of the merchant group saw the female demon, he immediately asked:

Who are you residing in the castle,
May I ask, why don't you come outside?
Quickly come out, mistress,
Let me admire your mighty power.

The female demon replied:

I'm miserable and naked
I don't dare to step out because I'm shy
Covering my body with my hair,
Because we rarely create good karma.

Merchant:

I will give you the clothes,
Put on and cover yourself, dear beauty,
Step out, mistress, I wish to
See you with enough divine power.

Demon girl:

Whatever you give me
It won't help me.
But here there is a disciple
Full of faith in Buddha.
After giving this person a shirt,
Dedicating to me this merit,
I will be given much happiness
All sources of pleasure will be filled.

You compile the scriptures and recite three verses to explain this:

After bathing him, the rich merchants
soaked the layman with incense oil,
And allowed him to wear clothes,
The female demon enjoyed the merit of the offerings.

This result is due to the offerings.
Filled with clothes and food.
Dressed elegantly, she is pure
Dressed in heavenly silk of Paramita

Smiling, the beautiful woman
stepped out of that floor and said:
"This is the result of the merit
The offerings you have offered".

Merchant:

The castle has many noble styles,
Lovely and cheerful, bright and clear,
Goddess 2 told the traveling group
What karma will result for her?

Goddess:

Meeting a mendicant on a journey,
True bhikkhu, faithful and faithful,
I came to offer him chestnut cakes
Mixing sesame oil with my own hands.

Because of this good karma, I enjoy it
In the castle for so many days
As a result of merit,
But it won't be long in this place.

After these four months are almost here,
Then we will meet Da Ma Than 3
Descending to the harsh hell,
I will suffer the most terrible fate.

The prison has four corners and four entrances,
It is divided into small, proportionate parts,
It is surrounded by iron walls,
And iron covers the top of the high roof.

The iron platform is blazing with fire,
Hot and dazzling in all ten directions,
Hell forever stands forever,
Spreads for hundreds of yojanas.

There I have suffered for a long time
The results are due to my ripe karma,
So I mourn and mourn forever
This story truly never goes away.

The lay disciple's heart was filled with emotion and compassion, he said:

-Hey goddess, thanks to the power of your offerings to me, you have fulfilled all your wishes. But now, by making offerings to these lay people and remembering all the virtues of the guru, she will escape rebirth in hell. The goddess was extremely happy, treating you with all kinds of food, clothes, magical jewels and giving you a set of robes to offer to the World-Honored One. She respectfully bowed and said:

-Please come to Sàvatthì and pay homage to the World-Honored One with these words I send: "World-Honored One, there is a female demon bowing to the World-Honored One's feet."

Then, thanks to her divine power, she brought the boat to the port that day. Those merchants came on time to offer gifts to the Buddha and told the above story.

Comment:

The woman in this story lived an evil life, but thanks to the good deed of offering a cake to a saint with a joyful heart, she was able to enjoy a piece of happiness in a castle in the middle of the ocean. At the same time, she had to endure the torture of living naked and cold with her hair covering her body as retribution for stealing clothes in her past life.

When good fate came, she met a group of merchants who were lay disciples of the Buddha and asked them to make offerings and direct that merit to help her escape the misery she had to endure for an entire lifetime. After that, the Buddha's faithful disciple showed her how to make offerings to a group of merchants and remember all the merits of the Master to escape rebirth in hell due to her previous evil deeds.

What is worth noting here is that in special cases where there are no true monks, lay disciples with full devotion and devotion can make offerings to the Three Jewels and dedicate the merit to the demons to bring blessings for them to enjoy.

(Excerpt from the monthly magazine Giac Ngo, No. 45, December 1999)

tieu_de: Story of the Lotus Root and Lotus Flower
tom_tat: The Story of the Lotus Root and the Lotus Flower (No. 392, Bhisapuppha's Birthplace) "You are not allowed to smell the scent of flowers..." The Master told this story while staying at the Jetavana Park about a Bhikkhu. The story goes that the Bhikkhu left the park and lived in Kosala for nearly a year
noi_dung:
The Story of Lotus Roots and Lotus Flowers

(No. 392, Precursor Bhisapuppha)

"You are not allowed to smell the flowers..."

The Master told this story while staying at the Jetty about a Bhikkhu. The story is that the Bhikkhu left the park and stayed in Kosala country near a forest. One day, he went down to the lotus pond. When he saw a lotus flower, he stood out of the wind and smelled the scent of the lotus. The goddess in that forest threatened him:

-Hey Venerable, you steal incense, this is a form of theft.

-Hey Bhikkhu, where have you been for a long time?

-World-Honored One, I was in that forest and the goddess threatened me like that.

The Master said:

-He was not the first person to be threatened by the goddess when smelling flowers. The wise men of the past were also threatened in the same way. And at the request of that Bhikkhu, he told the story of the past.

Once upon a time, when King Brahmadat I reigned in Banares (Pala Complaint), the Bodhisattva was born into a Brahmin Kàsi family. When he grew up, he studied the arts at Takkhasi and later became an ascetic living near a lotus pond. One day he stepped into the pond and stood smelling a blooming flower. A goddess in a nearby tree hole recited the first verse to threaten him:

1. You are not allowed to smell the scent of flowers,
Even if only one flower blooms,
That is truly the form of a thief,
Monks, you steal the scent of flowers.

The Bodhisattva immediately recited the second verse:

2. I don't pick or break the flowers,
The scent I smell comes from afar,
I can't tell you the reason
You said I was stealing the flowers.

At the same time, there was a person digging up lotus roots and lotus roots, breaking the lotus stem. Bodhisattva saw that and immediately said:

-She called a person who smelled a scent from afar a thief. Why don't you say that to the other person?

So he recited the third verse to talk about this:

3. That person is digging up the lotus root,
Breaking the broken tree trunk, look there,
Why don't you tell her how to act
That person is wanton and vile?

The goddess immediately recited the fourth and fifth verses to explain why she did not tell the other person:

4. Those who are dissolute, live carelessly,
Like a nanny's clothes, tired of living,
I don't say anything to that person,
But I only condescend to say it to you.

5. When you give up the desires of the world,
And seek the right concentration of body and mind,
Sins even as small as a tip of hair
are no different from the dark clouds in the sky!

Hearing such a warning from the goddess, the Bodhisattva was moved to recite the sixth verse:

6. Obviously the goddess clearly understood,
So for me, she took pity on me,
If you see me committing the same mistake again,
Please tell me more, I beg you.

After that, the goddess recited the seventh verse:

7. I don't live here to serve you,
We don't rent to anyone,
Please find your own way to
Supreme happiness in this world.

After encouraging him like that, the goddess returned to her residence. The Bodhisattva enthusiastically entered great samadhi and was later reborn in the Brahma world.

The Dharma talk ended, the Master proclaimed the Noble Truths and identified the previous incarnations: at the end of the Noble Truths, the Bhikkhu was established in the first fruition (Sotāpanna). At that time, the goddess was Uppalavanna (Lotus) and the ascetic was Me.

Comment:

This is a previous story related to the Buddha's teachings on how to maintain mindfulness and awareness in all actions of a Bhikkhu.

On the occasion of a young Bhikkhu smelling a lotus flower by the lake, a goddess appeared and reminded him not to steal the flower like that without asking anyone's permission.

He immediately reported it to the Buddha and he taught that in the past, when he was a Bodhisattva practicing in the forest, he was also warned by a goddess about similar behavior.

At that time, the Bodhisattva compared his behavior with the behavior of a person who was indiscriminately breaking off lotus stems and single-petaled lotus roots, then asked why the goddess did not warn him. The goddess explained: For those mortals who have not heard the Dharma and are still indulging in all the sensual pleasures of life, she does not want to remind them because they have committed many other mistakes that could be much bigger, so even being reminded is useless.

As for the Bhikkhus who have vowed to become a monk, leaving behind all worldly pleasures, they must always be careful in every action and gesture to be able to live a holy life "completely pure and white as a snail shell" in accordance with the Buddha's teachings so that they can diligently advance on the path of liberation and enlightenment. Therefore, they need to clearly see the danger in small mistakes to avoid committing big mistakes that can hinder them. step on your path of self-cultivation. However, that warning is only given once and then he must consciously control himself and no one reminds him again and again; Because becoming a monk is the personal wish of each person. Therefore, if he wants to achieve supreme happiness, he must regularly protect the purity of the three karma of body, speech and mind.

This sutra is classified in the Samyutta series in the Devas chapter. Here, the sutras were compiled by the monks and compiled into a story of previous lives in the form of prose interspersed with verses and questions and answers to increase the interest for students. The goddess here is the predecessor of Bhikkhuni Uppalavannà (Lotus), one of the two great female disciples of the Bhikkhuni Order who was given the title of female disciple with the highest supernatural power by the Buddha next to Bhikkhuni Khemà (Thai Hoa) - the first wisdom. Equal to the two Bhikkhus Sariputta (Sariputta) and Moggallàna (Moggallana), the first wisdom and the first supernatural powers in the Bhikkhu Sangha.

(Excerpt from the monthly magazine Giac Ngo, No. 66, September 2001)

noi_dung:
The story of King Loc's joy

( no. 385, Former Nandiyamiga )

"Brahman, did you enter the royal garden..."

The Master told this story at Jetavana about a Bhikkhu taking care of his mother. He asked the Bhikkhu:

-Is it true that he takes care of secular people?

-Yes, Venerable One.

-Who are they?

-World-Honored One, those are my parents.

-How good, how good! Bhikkhu, you maintain the precepts of the wise people of the past, because even when they were born as animals, they sacrificed their lives for their parents. And He told a story from the past.

Once upon a time, when the king of Kosala ruled over the people in Saketa (ie Oudh), the Bodhisattva was born as a deer. When he grew up, his name was Nandiyamiga (Hi Loc) with outstanding character and virtue. He took care of his parents.

At that time, King Kosala had a hobby of hunting, going into the forest every day with a large entourage, so the people could not do their farming and trading. They gathered together to discuss:

-Hey guys, our king is destroying our careers, our family life is withering away, so should we fence Anjanavana forest park, build a big gate, dig a lake and sow grass to grow, then go into the forest with sticks in hand, beat on the bushes, thus driving away the deer and bringing them into the forest park to live like cows in a stable? Then we close the gate, report it to the king and go about our business?

That's the way we have to do it. They told each other.

And they agreed to prepare the forest park, then enter the forest into a wide space, one mile on each side. At that time, Nandiya took her parents into a small bush and lay down on the ground. People holding wooden shields and weapons surrounded the bushes close together, a few people went in to search. Nai Nandiya saw them and immediately thought: "It's good that I will sacrifice my life today to save my parents." Thus, the deer stood up from his parents and said:

-Dear parents, these people will see all three of us if they enter the bush, there is only one way you can survive, and your life is paramount: I will sacrifice my life for you, by standing on the edge of the bush and running out as soon as they hit the bush, then they will think that there is only one small deer in this small bush, and will not go inside. So parents, please try to be very careful."

So the deer asked for permission to stand up and get ready to run out.

As ​​soon as the bush was banged and shouted by the people standing on the bank, the deer ran out, so they thought there was only one deer in there and did not go inside. Nandiya went with the group of deer, the group of people drove them into the forest, then they closed the gate and after reporting to the king, they returned home. From then on, the king always went to shoot the deer himself and brought the deer back himself or sent someone to find it and bring it back.

The deer herd prepared to wait for their turn. Whichever deer had its turn had to stand aside, then they took it away when it was shot dead. Nandiya kept drinking water from the lake and eating grass, but it wasn't her turn yet. Many days later, his parents wanted to see their child and immediately thought: "My son Nandiya is a king of fortune, as strong as an elephant and completely robust. If he were still alive, he would definitely jump the fence to visit us."

So the two of them stood on the side of the road. As soon as they saw a Brahmin, they asked in a human voice:

-Venerable sir, where are you going?

-Go to Sàketa. He replied.

Hearing that, the two of them wanted to leave a few words for me so they recited the first verse:

Brahmin, You entered the royal garden,
When you passed through Oudh, the capital,
Please find my beloved Nan-di,
And send a few words of truth,
After many years of exhaustion, parents are exhausted,
Longing for their child's return.

The Brahman said:

-Very good! And accepted.

The next day, he went to Sàketa, entered the royal garden and asked loudly:

-Who is Nandiya?

The deer king approached him and said:

-Here I am.

The Brahmin repeated the message, Nandiya heard that and replied:

-Hey Brahmin, I can leave. Surely we can jump the fence and escape. But I enjoy the king's food and drink, and that is like a debt to me. Besides, I have lived with this herd of deer for so long, it would not be reasonable for me to go without benefiting the king and the deer, or without proving my strength. So when it's my turn, I will benefit both people and animals, then return happily.

To explain this he recited two verses:

I thank the king, eat and drink abundantly,
I can't go yet, waiting for the time when I can do something useful
In front of the king's palace, I will wait with my ribs raised,
Then I will return to visit my parents to explain myself.

The Brahmin heard this and left.

Then, on the day it was the queen deer's turn, the king and his large entourage entered the royal garden. Bodhisattva stood aside. The king said:

-I will shoot this deer.

And the king attached a sharp arrow to the bowstring.

Bodhisattvas do not run away like other deer when afraid of death, but are filled with courage and take love as their guide. He stood still, displaying his strong ribs.

Due to the motivation of compassion, the king could not release the arrow. Bodhisattva said:

-Your Majesty, why don't you shoot? Please shoot.

-Hey king, I can't shoot.

-Your Majesty, then please consider the merits of those who keep the precepts.

Then the king was delighted with the Bodhisattva's words, immediately dropped his bow and said:

-Your Majesty, you give me peace, but what about all the deer in this garden?

-I will give them peace too. Thus, after creating peace for all the deer in the forest, the birds in the sky and the fish in the water, in the way described in the previous Nigrodhamiga (no. 12), the Bodhisattva made the king abide in the five precepts and said:

-O king, it is good for a king to rule the country by abandoning all evil ways, not violating the "Ten Kings Dharma" (ten virtues of a king) and acting righteously:

Almsgiving, kindness, virtue, justice,
Kindness, meekness, gentleness, patience,
Repentance, compassion are the ten moral precepts
I see that they are always solid in the mind.
From there arises the word grace
It is perfect and peaceful within the body.

Along with these words, he clearly stated all the virtues of a good king through the form of a verse.

After staying with the king for a few days, he ordered a golden drum to go throughout the capital, announcing the promise of peace for all living things. Then he said:

-Please, Your Majesty, please be careful to protect yourself.

Then he left to visit his parents.

Once upon a time I was the king of fortune in the land of Oudh,
Happy nature and name, Nan-di
Wanted to kill me in the royal garden, one day
The king came, the arrow lay still on the wire,
I exposed my ribs to the king who wanted to shoot
Then I went back to visit my parents to explain myself.

These are verses arising from the Supreme Wisdom of the Buddha.

At the end of the Dharma talk, the Master proclaimed the noble truths and identified previous incarnations. At the end of the Noble Truths, the Bhikkhu who takes care of his parents has already settled into the first fruition. At that time, my parents were the father and mother in the royal family, the Brahmin was Sariputta (Sariputta), the king was Ānanda (Ananda) and I was that King of Deer.

Comment:

Normally, a Bhikkhu leaves home without worldly consequences so that he can concentrate on cultivating the path of liberation and enlightenment. However, if he has elderly and helpless parents, he can also take care of his parents without being reprimanded by the Buddha as many people mistakenly think and tell him that story. On the contrary, when he heard the story of a Bhikkhu still taking care of his elderly parents, He also praised that filial conduct and advised his fellow monks not to be dissatisfied, and then, He told stories from the past proving that filial piety is one of the best virtues of intelligent sentient beings, and that even when he was in the animal life, the Bodhisattva also set a noble and shining example to inspire all beings, especially humans.

Filial piety is indeed a characteristic of intelligent beings, so it is very rare to see ordinary animals that only have the instinct to love their children. However, the previous Bodhisattva Buddha, with his great compassion to save all sentient beings, demonstrated that characteristic through many different forms of reincarnation, typically the form of the deer queen Joy in this previous life.

When he heard that the king wanted to shoot a deer to eat, the Bodhisattva tried to deceive the hunter so that his parents could escape, while he still happily waited for the day of execution and did not run away. Even though the queen deer had enough intelligence and strength to escape the siege in the royal garden, he still stayed there to wait for the opportunity to repay the king for giving him food and drink for a period of time, and at the same time he could use his kindness to educate the king and save the entire herd of deer.

Due to the Bodhisattva's compassionate motivation towards all living things, he showed extreme courage in front of the king's arrow that was ready to rush forward. The king could not shoot the deer as planned. On the contrary, the king felt regretful for his long-standing malice toward animals, so he ordered all species in his kingdom to be spared.

After that, the king received the Bodhisattva to abide in the five precepts, abandoning evil paths, and he taught him the Ten Kings Dharma to rule the country with the dignity of a wise king, doing good deeds all his life to bring peace and happiness to the people and be reborn in a good world in the next life.

And the story ends with the safe return of the Bodhisattva next to his parents in the joy of all beings.

(Excerpt from Giac Ngo Monthly Magazine No. 60, March 2001)

tom_tat: The Story of the Beautiful Lady Sulasà (no. 419, Sulasà's predecessor) "This is a golden bracelet..." The master told this story while staying at the park, about a maid of Anathapindika. The story goes that on a festival day, when she was about to come with her servants
noi_dung:
The Story of the Lady Sulasà

(number 419, Former Sulasà)

"Hey, this is a gold bracelet..."

The master told this story while staying at the monastery, about a maid of Anathapindika.

The story goes that on a festival day, when she was about to go with her servants to a pleasure garden, she asked the female owner Phuoc Tuong to give her a piece of jewelry to wear. The landlady gave her a piece of her jewelry worth one hundred thousand coins. She put it around her neck and went with the servants to the entertainment place.

A thief wanted that jewelry, with the intention of killing her to steal it, he came to talk to her in that garden. He fed her fish and meat and strong wine. She thought: "I'm sure he did that because he liked me." In the evening when everyone lay down to rest after all the fun, she got up to go find him. He said:

-Hey lady, this place is not private, let's go a little further.

She thought: "Anything secret can happen here. Surely he wants to kill me and take the jewelry I'm wearing. So I will teach him a lesson." So she said: - Dear Sir, I am thirsty and my throat is dry from drinking strong wine. Please find me some water.

Then taking him to the well, she told him to draw water and showed him the rope and bucket. The thief dropped the bucket. Then as soon as he bent down to pull the water up, the maid, who was very strong, pushed him hard with her hands and knocked him into the well. She said:

-You won't die from this method.

Then she threw a large brick on his head. He died immediately on the spot. When she returned to the city and returned the jewelry to the landlady, she said:

-I was almost killed today because of that jewelry.

Then she told the whole story. The landlady then told the story to Anathapindika and he reported it to the Tathagata. The master said:

-Hey homeowner, this is not the first time that maid has had timely intelligence, it was the same in the past. This is not the first time she has killed that person, but has also killed that person before.

And according to Anathapindika, he told a story from the past.

Also in this capital, there was a robber named Sattuka, as strong as an elephant, who often broke into rich houses at night to rob as much as he wanted. The people in the city gathered to report the accusations to the king.

The king ordered guards stationed everywhere to capture robbers and behead them. They tied his hands behind his back and led him to the execution ground while whipping him all over the place. At that time, Sulasà stood by the window looking down the street, saw the bandit suddenly falling in love with him and thought: "If I can save this strong soldier from danger, I will give up my current evil life and live righteously with him." She regained his freedom by sending a thousand gold coins to the mayor and then lived happily in harmony with him. After about three or four months, the robber thought: "I will never be able to stay in a place like this, but I cannot leave empty-handed. Sulasà's jewelry is worth a hundred thousand coins. I want to kill her and take the loot."

So one day he told her:

- Dear lady! While I was being dragged away by the king's soldiers, I promised to make an offering to a tree spirit on the top of the mountain, and now he is threatening me for not returning the offering. So let's go make offerings to the gods.

- Dear husband! Very well, let's prepare offerings to send to the gods.

- Hey lady! Sending offerings to the gods won't have any effect. Let's go to Mass together, bringing all our personal belongings and attendants.

- Dear husband! okay, let's do it together.

He told her to prepare the offerings and when they reached the foot of the mountain, he said:

She agreed and he told her to bring the vase. He had prepared very carefully. When the two reached the top of the mountain, he placed the offering at the base of a tree growing next to the cliff that was a hundred times taller than a normal person and said:

-Hey lady, I didn't come here to offer an offering, but came here with the intention of killing you and escaping with all your belongings, so take them all off and put them in a bundle in your coat.

-Hey prince, why do you want to kill me?

-For her money.

-My lord, remember all the good things I have done for you: When you were chained hand and foot and dragged to be beheaded, I left a rich guy just for you and paid a large sum of money to redeem you. Even if I could earn a thousand coins a day, I wouldn't look at any other man. I have become your benefactor like that. Please don't kill me. I vow to give you a lot of money and be your slave.

Along with these supplications, she recited the first verse:

1. Here is the golden bracelet,
Here is the jade and the pearl necklace,
Take it all away from me
Please let me be your servant!

Sattuka then recited the second verse in accordance with his purpose, which is:

2. Put the gold and pearls on the lovely lady,
And don't you cry and be sad
I want to kill you right now
Because I'm not sure about the dowry.

3. Through all the years of growing up
With so many true memories in my soul,
I swear in this mortal world
No one has been closer to me than you.

4. Come here one last time
I bow in your arms
Never in this life
From now on we meet, my dear!

Sattuka could not understand her purpose, so he said:

-Very well, my dear, come and hold me in your arms.

Sulasa walked around him, respectfully bowed three times, kissed him and said:

-Hey prince, now I bow to you from the side.

She placed her head on his feet, bowed to both sides, then walked around behind him as if she was about to bow to him there; Then with the strength of an elephant, she grabbed his legs and threw him upside down into the abyss of death a hundred times higher than an ordinary person. he disintegrated and died on the spot.

Seeing this, the god on top of the mountain recited the following verses:

5. Wisdom is also very common
Not reserved for men,
Women can be very wise
Appear in dangerous situations.

6. Wisdom is also very common
Not reserved for boys
Girls are quick-witted and have many plans
Plan to do the job on time.

7. She showed her wisdom
Knowing all the ways,
Killed the guy like a snake
Killed the deer with a drawn bow.

8. A person who, when faced with a dead end situation,
Cannot climb up to escape
Will fall like a stupid thief
Falling into the bone-shattering abyss.

9. But those who are quick to see the situation
Danger coming to their fate,
Like she was able to escape from
The terrifying enemy at her side.

So Sulasà killed that robber. When she came down the mountain and stood among the servants, she asked where her husband was. She said:

-Stop asking me!

Then climbing into the car, she went straight to the capital.

Comment:

These two previous stories have nothing to do with two young women who fell in love at first sight with two ferocious bandits, wanderers at the end of their lives, and the two women wanted to save their lives to live together in the future. But both girls had to pay a very high price for their adventurous actions even though each person was in a different situation and position.

Little Gunner's wife was originally a well-mannered girl who was taught by her father, a famous professor throughout the world, from a young age within the framework of rites so that she could become a good wife, and then he chose a husband for his daughter who was the most worthy student among his disciples. But her personality quickly changed unusually with the pain of blind, intense passion. Forgetting the ethics of being a wife, she cruelly plotted to kill her husband to satisfy her temporary desires. And she reaped the disastrous results of that foolish action right after that. However, she still could not see her mistakes in the way she behaved and planned to continue living in evil ways, so Sakka, the incarnation of the Bodhisattva, had to disguise herself on earth to perform a tragic comedy to teach her to repent of her sins and correct herself in the future.

But that bandit was used to living a wandering life here and there, so he couldn't limit himself to a normal family life forever. Then his old violent nature emerged, causing him to forget his wife, who was the benefactor who saved his life not long ago. And so, he plotted to kill her to take her property before setting off again. Even when she begged him to spare her life and was willing to surrender all her assets and become his slave, he still did not give up his intention to betray her.

For a conscience-stricken man who didn't know it was like that, Sulasà's only way to save herself was to kill him. Intelligence appeared to help her think of a plan to deceive him to avoid disaster for herself. Her wise and courageous timely action to eliminate time and violence and free herself from that dangerous situation was praised by the Bodhisattva at that time, the mountain god who witnessed the story and recited inspirational verses. Just like in the story of the previous life of the leopard, for those cruel creatures that do not know reason, the Buddha also praised people or animals with enough intelligence and courage to resist them to protect themselves.

(Excerpt from Giac Ngo Monthly magazine No. 69, December 2001)

tom_tat: King Dalha-dhamma's story (409. Dalha-dhamma's predecessor) "I was the porter from the green day..." The master told this story while staying in the Ghosita forest near Kosambi, about Bhaddavatika, the female elephant of King Udena. Now
noi_dung:
The story of King Dalha-dhamma

(409. Precursor Dalha-dhamma)

"I was the porter from the green day..."

The master told this story while staying in the Ghosita forest near Kosambi, about Bhaddavatika, the female elephant of King Udena.

Now the way this elephant was decorated with gold and jade and the story of King Udena's family will be mentioned in the Mamtanga Jataka (no. 497). One day, this elephant went out to the outskirts of the city early in the morning to meet the Buddha surrounded by Saints, in the supreme majesty of an Enlightened One, entering the city to beg for alms. He knelt down at the Tathagata's feet, lamented and prayed to Him:

-World-Honored One, the omniscient one, the savior of suffering throughout the world, when I was young and capable of working, King Udena, a wise man, loved me and said: "My life, along with the kingdom and the queen, are all thanks to him." Then he bestowed great glory on me by adorning it with gold and jewels, he ordered the elephant's cage to be plastered with soil mixed with spices, hanging brightly colored objects around it, lighting lamps with fragrant oil, placing a plate of incense there, he also ordered a golden basin to be placed at the place where I defecated, made me stand on a colored carpet and fed me all the king's finest delicacies. Now I'm old and can't work anymore, so you took away all those privileges, I live alone and miserable with no one to protect and take care of me, I only eat ketaka fruit in the forest, I have no refuge anymore. Please tell King Udena to reconsider my merits and restore all my former glory.

The master said:

-You go home, then I will tell the king to restore all your former glory.

Then he went to the royal palace door.

The king invited the Buddha in and gave a grand reception to all the congregation who followed the Buddha. When the meal was over, the Master spoke words of joy and merit and asked:

-Your Majesty, where is the elephant Bhaddavatikà?

-World-Honored One, I don't know.

-Your Majesty, after giving glory to your servants, it is not ethical for you to take away all favors when they are old and weak, so it is reasonable to show gratitude to them. Bhaddavatikà is now old, worn out by age and unprotected by anyone, living only on Ketaka fruit in the forest. It is not reasonable for the Great King to leave him helpless like that when he is old and weak.

Then recounting the merits of the elephant Bhaddavatikà, he said:

-Your Majesty, please restore all its former glory.

And then he left. The king did as he was told. The whole capital spread the news that its old glory had been restored thanks to the Buddha recounting all its merits.

This matter was discussed by the Sangha during the meeting. The Master came in and heard that this was your topic. He said:

-Hey Bhikkhus, this is not the first time Tathagata has restored it to all its former glory by telling stories of its merits.

And He told a story from the past.

Once upon a time, there was a king named Dalhadhamma who ruled in Ba La Nai. At that time, the Bodhisattva was born into the family of the most important mandarin in the court. The king had a very brave and strong female elephant. It traveled one hundred miles a day, doing all the duties of the king's envoy. When it went into battle, it fought fiercely, crushing the enemy. The king often said:

-This elephant is very useful to me.

Then the king gave it all the adornments and glory like King Udena gives to Bhaddavatikà today. Then when he got old and weak, the king took away all of the above privileges.

Since then it has not been protected by anyone and has only lived on grass and leaves in the forest. One day, the ceramics in the king's palace were not enough, so the king ordered the potters to say:

-Pottery is not enough.

The king heard the story and immediately said:

-Where is my female elephant?

-Your Majesty, it is wandering at will.

The king told him to give it to the potter:

-From now on, you tie it to the car and take it to transport fertilizer.

The potter replied:

-Your Majesty, that's very good.

Then he did as told. One day, while out in the city, the female elephant suddenly saw the Bodhisattva coming, immediately knelt down at his feet, crying and saying:

-Dear prime minister, when I was young, the king considered me very useful and gave me great glory, now that I am old and weak, he has taken away all privileges and no longer thinks of me, I have no one to protect me and only live on grass and leaves in the forest, I am in such dire straits, you give me to the potter to tie me to a dung cart; Except for the prime minister, I have no one to rely on. The prime minister himself knows all my efforts in serving the king. Please let me restore all the glory I have lost.

Then the female elephant recited three verses :

It was I who carried it from day one
So the king is satisfied?
I carry all the weapons on my chest
Charging into battle, walking heroically.

You have accomplished many victories.
The king must have forgotten now.
How many times have you served many merits
As was appointed for the messengers?

Now I am alone, so helpless.
Surely my end has come.
Serving for the potter's house
I have no choice but to be a squeegee.

The Bodhisattva heard the story, immediately comforted it and said:

-Stop being sad, I will go report to the king and restore all your honor.

So when he entered the city, he went to the king after breakfast and began the story, he said:

-Your Majesty, did the female elephant by that name go to battle in certain places with weapons strapped to her chest, and then another day she carried her credentials around her neck and traveled hundreds of miles as a messenger for the king, and the king gave her much glory, where is she now?

-I gave it to the potter who carried the cow dung.

The Bodhisattva immediately replied:

Due to personal selfish desires,
People bestow all glory
Like you to that elephant,
Throw away like a weak slave

When people forget all their merits.
The good deeds of the past enjoy a full share
Everything that the heart is planning
The future will surely perish.

When people remember their deeds
The good deeds of the past are fully enjoyed
Everything that the heart is planning
The next day will surely succeed

I speak the perfect truth
For the people to gather around
Always remember old deeds
Heaven reserves a glorious life

With this opening statement, the Bodhisattva precepted all the people gathered there. Hearing this, the king immediately gave the old elephant all its old glory. And later, following the Bodhisattva's teachings, the king gave alms and practiced many other good deeds, so he was born in the Heavenly realm.

When the dharma talk ended, the master recognized his previous incarnation: "At that time, the female elephant was Bhaddavatikà, the king was Ananda, the great minister was me."

Comment :

Gratitude is one of the important themes of the Jataka Tales. Gratitude to people or things that have done good deeds for us was promoted by the Buddha through many previous stories and this story is an example. Taking advantage of the story of King Udena's mistreatment and abandonment of the old and weak elephant, who had performed many glorious deeds for the king during his youth and had been given many honors and benefits by the king, the Master advised the king to let it restore all its former glory, and He told a story from the past that proved that in a previous life, He had done a similar thing.

Moreover, he also taught his disciples to be grateful to all the beneficial plants and trees around them. In many other past lives, He taught that when we sit under a tree that gives us shade even for a moment, we also show gratitude by not breaking branches and picking leaves, because only evil people will harm good friends.

This is shown immediately after attaining enlightenment. In the endless joy of liberation, He constantly admired the ancient Asattha tree, or banyan tree (Nigrodha), a type of fig tree, to show gratitude to the tall tree that gave Him a solid place to stay during the final battle against the Demon King and the Demon Army who rushed to attack Him like a storm before He became the heroic victor. According to Venerable Narada, a famous magician in the Buddhist world, this attitude of the Buddha indirectly taught humanity a great moral lesson. Later, following his example, his disciples also respected that ancient tree and its descendants and they were named the Bodhi tree to commemorate his enlightenment.

When the Buddha decided to preach the Dharma to save living beings after many weeks of enjoying the peace and joy of immortal Nirvana, he immediately thought of the two masters Àlàra Kàlàma and Uddaka Ràmaputta who had guided him on the path of learning; Then followed by the group of six ascetics Komdanna, fellow practitioners, who served him during the period when he practiced the first ascetic methods but did not bring enlightenment and liberation, and they left him before he alone followed the new path of practicing meditation under that Bodhi tree.

During his time on earth as well as in ancient stories, the Buddha always advocated gratitude. He rejected the act of ingratitude and ingratitude, because he clearly saw that it was evil karma that could lead to ruin in this life and rebirth in the lower realms of hell; Repaying gratitude means good karma, which will lead to prosperity and success in this life and good rebirth in the next life. Buddha's teachings on gratitude for the good deeds we receive from people, things, and even plants and trees are extremely noble and have practical benefits for humanity today.

In history, never before have people around the world tried to destroy the living environment in modern times. Due to endless greed, people find ways to deplete natural resources through cutting down trees, destroying forests, causing forest fires... causing serious floods in large areas of land or hunting rare animals for fur, skin, horns, tusks, honey,... creating the risk of extinction for some animals like the king in the story of the Great Monkey King who planned to destroy the habitat and make extinct the entire family of 80,000 monkeys, just because of a little greed. my selfish taste! While wanting to satisfy the endless desires of individuals or groups, they do not think about the harmful consequences for the surrounding environment as well as for themselves in this life and the next.

Stemming from immeasurable compassion for all living beings, Buddhist ethics are ideal for ecological environmental ethics. We can affirm that Buddhist life is very close to the natural environment. Never like now, we need to apply and spread Buddha's teachings on gratitude more widely so that more and more people are aware of the need to protect the earth, a planet often compared to a gentle mother that provides rich natural resources for all living creatures. If we humans do not know how to respect and protect the current living environment, the negative consequences will be unpredictable for future generations and disaster for the ecological environment is inevitable, because up to now, mother earth is still the only green planet that provides a source of life for all living creatures according to the discoveries of modern science.

(Excerpt from the monthly magazine Giac Ngo, No. 63, June 2001)

tieu_de: Story of the Great Bodhi Tree and Sacred King Kāliṅga
tom_tat: The story of the Great Bodhisattva and the Holy Emperor Kàlinga (Predecessor Kàlinga - Bodhi) This story was told by the Master while staying at Jetavana, about Venerable Ananda performing the offering ceremony to the Bodhi tree. While the Tathagata traveled for the purpose of receiving people
noi_dung:
The Story of Great Bodhisattva and the Holy Emperor Kàlinga

(Forerunner of Kàlinga - Bodhi)

While the Tathagata was traveling for the purpose of accepting those who had the opportunity to receive precepts, the people of Savatthi approached Ky Vien, holding fragrant wreaths in their hands. Seeing that there was no other place to show their admiration and devotion, they persistently placed flowers at the entrance to the Buddha's 4th Fragrance Room and then left. This caused great joy. But the rich man Anathapindika heard about it; When the Tathagata returned, the rich man went to visit the Venerable Ānanda and told him: "Venerable sir, this monastery was not offered offerings while the Tathagata was traveling, and there was no place for people to offer fragrant flowers to show their devotion. Please, Venerable One, kindly tell the Tathagata about this matter so that he can let you know if we can find a place to use for this purpose?". The other Venerable was ready to do so, so he immediately asked the Buddha: "World-Honored One, how many types of Stupas are there?".

- Hey Ananda, there are three types.

- World-Honored One, what are these types?

- Stupas worshiping the golden body, Stupas worshiping objects commonly used or carried on the body, and Stupas worshiping other souvenirs 5.

- While the World-Honored One is still alive, is it possible to build a Stupa?

- No, Ānanda, it is impossible to build a Stupa to worship the golden body, that type of stupa can only be built when a Buddha passes away. A Stupa enshrining a souvenir is also not right because the relationship depends entirely on the mind. The Great Bodhi tree has been used by the Buddhas, so it is very worthy as a place of worship, whether the Buddhas are still in this world or passed away.

- World-Honored One, while the World-Honored One was traveling far away, this great Ky Vien Monastery had no place to rely on, and the people had no place to express their devotion. Please, World-Honored One, allow me to plant a seed from the Maha Bodhi tree (in Bodh Gaya) right in front of the gate of this Monastery? - Of course we should do so, Ananda, and it will also be a place of refuge for Me like before.

This Venerable told the story again to the Venerable Anathapindika, Mrs. Visakka 6 and King Kosala. Then at the gate of Ky Vien monastery, the Venerable dug a hole to plant a Bodhi tree and said to the Great Elder Moggallàna (Moggallana):

- I want to plant a Bodhi tree in front of Ky Vien monastery, can you please find a Bodhi tree for me?

The elder readily agreed and immediately flew through space to the land of the Bodhi tree. He placed under his robe a Bodhi fruit that was falling from the tree trunk but did not fall to the ground, and brought it back to give to Venerable Ānanda. This monk informed King Kosal that he was about to plant a Bodhi tree. So in the afternoon the king arrived with a large group of entourage, then Mr. Anathapindika and Ms. Visàkà also arrived with a group of devotees.

Where the Bodhi tree was about to be planted, Venerable Ānanda placed a golden vase, with a hole in the bottom, filled with soil soaked in fragrant water. The Venerable said:

- Your Majesty, please plant this Bodhi seed.

Then give that seed to the king. But the king thought that this kingdom could not stay in his hands forever, so he let Anathapindika plant it, and immediately gave the seeds to the rich man. Then Anathapindika dug up the fragrant soil and put the seeds in. Just as the seed fell from his hand, right in front of everyone's eyes, a young Bodhi tree, about the size of a plowshare head, about fifty cubits high (1 cubit = 0.45m) sprouted from all sides five large branches 50 cubits long, like the trunk of that tree. The tree standing tall like that is truly a lord of the forest, a rare and magical miracle! The king sprinkled golden and silver vases around the tree trunk, a total of eight hundred vases filled with fragrant water, beautiful and filled with countless blue lotus flowers. As always, the king ordered to place a long row of bowls filled with food and a throne made of seven treasures, sprinkled with gold, then build a wall around that area, and build a gate guard house made of seven treasures. The King expressed such special and solemn devotion to the Bodhi tree.

The Venerable Ananda said again:

The Master immediately used the place where the Bodhi tree had just been planted to enter samadhi all night long.

At that time, the Sangha began to talk about the above matter at the Dharma Hall:

- Dear friends, while the Tathagata was still alive, Venerable Ānanda asked to plant a Bodhi tree and perform a great offering ceremony. The power of that Venerable is truly great!

The Master went in and asked the Sangha what they were discussing. You reported to Him. He said:

- Monks, this is not the first time Ananda has guided human assemblies across the four continents of the world and his large entourage to bring countless fragrant wreaths and open a Bodhi festival in the ashram around the Bodhi tree.

After speaking, He told a story from the past.

Once upon a time, in the kingdom of Kàlinga in the capital Dantapura, there was a king named Kàlinga. The king had two princes named Mahà-Kàlinga and Culla-Kàlinga. At that time, the prophets predicted that the crown prince would rule after his father's death, while his younger brother would become an ascetic, living a mendicant life, but his son would later become a Holy Chakravarti King 7.

Time passed when his father passed away, the crown prince ascended the throne, and his younger brother became Viceroy. The royal brother thought that his son would one day become a Holy Chakravartin King, so he became arrogant because of that. The king could not bear this and immediately ordered an envoy to arrest Viceroy Kalinga. The other messenger came and said:

- Your Highness, the Great King wants to arrest you, so please worry about saving your life.

The prince immediately showed the envoy assigned this important task the ring with his own mark, a beautiful carpet and a sword: There were three treasures in all. Then the prince said:

- Khanh must recognize my prince through these tokens and support him to the throne.

With the above instructions, the prince quickly fled into the forest. There he built a hermitage in a beautiful, pleasant place and lived like an ascetic on a river bank.

At that time in the kingdom of Madda in the capital Sagala, King Madda had just given birth to a princess. As for this princess, like the other prince, the prophets predicted that she would have to become an ascetic, but her son would become a Holy Chakravarti King. The kings in Jambudvipa (i.e. India) 8 heard that rumor and immediately came to besiege the capital.

The king thought to himself: "If I marry my daughter to any king, the other kings will be angry. So I must try to save my daughter's life." So the king, the queen and the princess hid in disguise into the forest, and after building a hermitage a little far from the river bank, above Prince Kàlinga's hermitage, they lived there like ascetic monks, eating all the fruits they could gather.

The two parents wanted their daughter to be safe, so they let her stay in the hut, then went out to pick wild fruits. While the two were away, she gathered all kinds of flowers to make a wreath. At that time, on the banks of the Ganges River, there was a mango tree in beautiful bloom, forming a natural ladder. She climbed up there, played and tried to drop the wreath into the water.

One day, Prince Kàlinga had just stepped out of the water after bathing when a wreath got stuck in his hair.

He looked at the flower and said to himself: "Some woman made this flower, but it was not an adult woman but a young girl. I have to go find her." So he fell in love and went upstream of the Ganges River, until he heard her singing in a sweet voice while sitting on a mango tree. He approached the tree, saw her, and said:

- Hey beauty, what kind of animal are you?

- Dear Sir, I am a person, she replied.

- Then go down, he said.

- Miss, me too, please step down.

- Dear Sir, no, I won't come down. Words do not make a Satsattva; If you are indeed a Satsattva, please tell me the secrets of that traditional ritual.

Afterwards, the two told each other the stories of their lineage. Then the princess stepped down and the two sides made friends.

When her parents returned, she told them the story of King Kalinga's son, why he had to go to the forest with all the details. The two agreed to marry her to him. While living together in harmony, the princess conceived and after ten months, she gave birth to a son with a good appearance and merit and named him Kalinga. The boy grew up, learning all kinds of talented arts from his father and grandfather.

Later, his father saw the combination of stars and knew that his brother had passed away. So he called his son in and said: - Son, you should not waste your life in the boring jungle, because my brother, the Great King Kalinga, has passed away. So you must return to Dantapura and inherit the kingship of our family.

After that, the father gave his son the things he brought with him: the ring with the signal, the carpet and the sword and said:

- My son, in the city of Dantapura over there, there is a god who is my trusted servant. Go to his house, go straight into his room, show him these three things and tell him that you are my child. He will put you on the throne.

The young man said goodbye to his parents and grandparents. Then, thanks to the divine power of his merit, he flew through space, went down to the mandarin's house, and went straight to his private room.

- Who is the young master?, the mandarin asked.

He replied:

- I am the son of Emir Kalinga.

Then pull out those three tokens. The mandarin immediately informed the royal palace, the courtiers immediately decorated the capital and raised the royal parasol over his head. Then the royal priest named Kàlinga - Bhàvadvàja taught him the Ten Dharmas that a Holy Chakravartin King must achieve and he learned all ten of them. Then, on a full moon day, the day of the precepts, from Cakkadaha appeared to the king the Treasured Wheel, from the Uposatha lineage appeared the Treasured Elephant, from the Valàha noble breed appeared the Treasured Horse, from Veppulla appeared the Jewel, then the Treasured Queen and her concubines and the Treasured Prince gradually appeared.

After that the king ruled the entire earth.

* * *

One ​​day, accompanied by his entourage for thirty-six miles, he sat on a white statue as high as the peak of Mount Kelasa. In a majestic and splendid scene, he returned to visit his parents in the old place. But when he wanted to cross the land around the Maha Bodhi tree, the glorious seat of the Buddhas, which had become the center of the universe, the precious elephant could not pass: the king kept pushing the elephant, but the elephant still could not pass.

To explain this, the Master recited the first verse:

1. Holy Emperor Kha Linh
King of Chakravarti,
True, he rules the earthly world,
Once upon a time he came to Bodhi,
On his body was a majestic and precious elephant.

Therefore, the court priest traveling with the king thought to himself: "There is nothing in space that hinders it, why can't the king urge the elephant to cross? I want to come and see." Descending from the sky, this person admired the glorious throne of the Buddhas, and the area around the Great Bodhi tree.

At that time, it was said that in about a mile of that pool, there was never a single blade of grass growing, not even the size of a hair, the ground was like fine sand, all four sides were herbs, auspicious plants, and great tho were like the lords of the forest standing tall as if admiring, their heads turned to face the Bodhi seat. When the Brahmin Priest observed this place, he thought: "This is the place where the Buddhas have eliminated all worldly desires, so no one can overcome it, even if it is Thich Thich Thien himself." And approaching the king, the Priest told him about the characteristics of the area around the Bodhi tree, and requested the Holy King to sit down on the elephant.

To explain this issue, the Master recited the following verses:

2. The Priest said to the Holy King,
As a son of a gentle ascetic family,
When you move the precious chakra,
After paying homage to him, he will guide you on the way:

3. This is the place where poets still praise,
Please come down and pay homage to King Hung,
Here are the supreme Buddhas
The perfect enlightenment radiates light.

4. Legend has it that in the mortal world
This is the sacred land of the gods,
Herbs, auspicious plants, and great longevity,
Standing around in an attitude of worship.

5. Come down here, please pay your respects solemnly,
Because you have come to a far away land,
On the great earth that nourishes all things,
This place is a holy and sacred land.

6. The king is full of all kinds of elephants
Purebred thanks to good parents,
If you come here, the elephants still want to
But they can't go near the place.

7. Sitting on its body is a pure-bred statue,
God's will is up to you, just push the elephant,
But there's no way the elephant can walk,
At this point, the elephant must stand still.

8. The king heard the prophet's words,
As he commanded the statue to go,
He pushed his stick deep into the statue:
"If this is so, I will see it immediately."

9. Being prodded, the elephant screams like a trumpet,
Like a sharp stork, a resounding crane
Shaking, immediately falling due to the force
Heavy on the side, unable to stand up.

Because the king kept pushing and prodding, the elephant could not stand the pain, so he had to die immediately. But the king did not know that the elephant was dead, so he calmly sat on the elephant's back. A moment later, Master Kàlinga - Bhàradmàja said:

The Master recited the tenth verse to explain this:

10. The national monk was afraid when he saw the elephant
Dead, his heart was shocked and he said:
"Please find another elephant, Your Majesty,
Your elephant has now died!".

Thanks to the Holy King's merit and divine power, another elephant of the Uposatha breed appeared before the king and offered his back. The king sat on its back. At that moment, the king's body immediately fell to the ground and disappeared.

The Master recited verses to explain this:

11. The king was frightened when he heard this incident.
He sat on another elephant, and suddenly
The corpse of the precious statue fell down.
The true words of prophecy were revealed.

Then the king descended from space and admired the land around the Bodhi tree. Faced with the miraculous event that had just appeared, the king praised the national teacher Bhàradvàja through verses:

12. Thus, to his Master Te,
The Great Emperor Kha Linh said: "Truly
You are knowledgeable and thorough in everything,
You have foreseen all dependent arising"

But at that time the Brahmin did not want to accept the above praise, but still maintained his humble position, he praised the merits of the Buddhas with all his words:

The Master again recited verses to explain the problem:

13. The national teacher refused the recognition
And said this to the Holy King:
"I only know signs and symptoms,
But the Buddhas are fully enlightened.

14. Buddha's knowledge and understanding reach all truth,
For signs, they do not pay attention,
Buddhas are omniscient through insight,
Gods are not profound scholars".

The king heard about the merits of the Buddhas, so his heart was filled with joy, and he immediately ordered mortals to bring many fragrant wreaths to make offerings to the land surrounding the Bodhi spirit for seven consecutive days and nights. The Master recited a couple of verses to explain this:

15. Holy Bodhisattva, the Lord offered offerings
With so much melodious music,
Beautiful and fragrant flower wreaths,
He built around a wall.

16. Then the Holy Emperor left,
Bringing sixty thousand carts full of flowers,
Making offerings, for the Great Emperor,
Kha Linh worshiped Bodhi Holy Land.

After performing the solemn offering ceremony for the Bodhisattva Bodhisattva as above, the king visited his parents, then took them back to Dantapura city to live with him. Here he specialized in giving alms and doing other duties, until his death when he was reborn in the Thirty-three Heaven.

After ending the Dharma talk, the Master said:

"Monks, this is not the first time Ananda has made offerings to the Bodhi tree, but it was the same in the past.

Then he identified his predecessor:

Comment:

After the Buddha attained enlightenment, he enjoyed liberation and nirvana for many weeks in the land that witnessed his enlightenment under the Assatha tree (a tree of the fig family) and he constantly admired the great old tree to silently thank the noble tree for protecting him during the time he fought fiercely to achieve Buddhahood. Following his example, Buddha's disciples also showed respect for this ancient tree and named it the Bodhi tree to symbolize the place where Buddha attained ultimate wisdom. Furthermore, the Sangha and lay disciples at that time unanimously requested the Buddha to allow them to bring a seed of that Bodhi tree and plant it right in Ky Vien as a symbol of enlightenment. And during the times when He traveled far away, the disciples there also had a special symbolic place to worship Him.

Since then, the Bodhi Festival proposed by Venerable Ànada has met the spiritual needs of Buddha's disciples. On the occasion of Venerable Ānanda being praised by the monks for his merits, the Buddha told a story of the previous incarnations that said that in the past Buddhas also achieved Enlightenment at Bodhi Holy Land, so it became a special place where all species from plants to creatures expressed their attitude of worship.

The Chakravarti king wanted to test the truth, so he continued to push the elephant forward, but the elephant fell over and died on the spot.

On the occasion of Buddha's Enlightenment and also the beginning of Spring, I would like to send to my friends near and far this noble and fragrant Jataka story to commemorate one of the four important relics that the Buddha left footprints on during his time in this world that today all Buddhists in all four directions pay their respects to: Lumbini (Lumbini) where the Buddha was born; Bodh Gaya, where he attained Enlightenment; Deer Park, where he first turned the wheel of Dharma, and Kusinara (Kushina) where he passed away in ultimate Nirvana.

In addition, Western scholars also see similarities in the details of Princess Madda dropping the wreath into the stream, leading to the fateful relationship between her and Prince Kalinga, as well as the details of royal signals to recognize the prince later in European fairy tales. Thus, once again, we clearly see the influence of these Buddha's previous lives spreading to many different cultures around the world./.

(Excerpt from the monthly magazine Giac Ngo, No. 70-71, February 1, 2002)

tieu_de: Story of the Great Parrot King
tom_tat: The story of Dai Anh Vu (429. Mahàsuka's predecessor) "Whenever the fruit tree gives birth" The Master told this story while staying at Jetavana about a Bhikkhu. The story goes that he lived in the forest near a border village in Kosala and received teachings from
noi_dung:
The Story of Dai Anh Vu

(429. Mahàsuka's predecessor)

"Whenever fruit trees bear fruit"

The Master told this story while staying at Jetavana about a Bhikkhu.

The story is that he lived in the forest near a border village in Kosala and
received instructions from the Master on meditation topics. The people made him a retreat in a place they often frequented, provided him with shelter day and night, and served him very attentively. In the
first month of his residence in the rainy season, that village was burned down and the people
did not have a grain of rice left, so they could not offer delicious food
in that alms bowl, so even though he lived in a comfortable place, he
was so sad due to lack of food that he could not enter the Holy Path or
Holy Fruition.

So when the three months of rain ended, he went to see the Master, after the words
Greeting warmly, the Master expressed his strange hope that despite the difficulty in providing food offerings, he would also have a comfortable place to stay. The Bhikkhu reported to Him how the situation had developed. When he heard that he had a peaceful residence, the Master said:

- Monks, if that is the case, an ascetic should abandon the
habits of greed, and be content with whatever food he receives in order to fulfill
the duties of a monk. The wise men of the past, when they were born as animals, even though they only lived on dust in the decaying tree where they lived, gave up all desires and knew how to live enough to stay there and fulfill the principle of kindness. Then why did he leave a peaceful residence just because the
food he received was too little and rudimentary?And at this person's request, He told
the story of the past.

* * *

Once upon a time there were countless parrots living in the Snow Mountain region on the banks of the Ganges River in a fig forest. That Vuong King encountered a time when the fruit on the tree he resided in was out of season. He had to eat whatever was left, whether it was sprouts, leaves, bark or tree trunks, and drank water from the Ganges River. He still found peace and contentment where he lived.

Due to this peaceful and contented mood, Sakka's throne shook. Sakka found out the cause and saw this bird. Then, wanting to test the bird's virtue, he used his divine power to make the tree wither, becoming a rotten tree trunk full of holes, standing alone, buffeted by wind and rain, and dust flying out of those holes!

Sakka God noticed that Vu lived a very contented life, so he said to himself: "After listening to the bird talk about the virtue of friendship, I will come and grant the bird a favor and cast a spell to make the fig tree bear immortal fruit." So he assumed the form of a swan with his queen Suja 9 in front, transforming into the goddess Asura. He went to that fig forest, perched on a nearby cluster of trees and recited verses to begin a conversation with Anh Vu:

1. Whenever a fruit tree bears fruit,
Flocks of hungry birds come to fill the branches,
But when the tree becomes withered,
Immediately the birds flee quickly.

After these words, he recited the verse again urging the bird to go away:

2. Hey Mr. Red Beak, go quickly
Are you still sitting daydreaming, why?
Tell me, spring bird,
Why are you clinging to that dry piece of wood?

The oriole replied: - Hey swan, out of gratitude, I will not leave this tree.

Then the bird recited two verses:

3. Those who have been close since spring,
Know clearly everything that is good and true,
Whether in life, death or suffering,
Never abandon their friends.

4. I want to be considerate and keep a good heart
With the tree that has been friends for many years,
I hope to live, even though I can't bear to
Leave the dry, dying tree.

Sakka heard the bird speak and was very happy. While praising the bird and wanting to grant the bird a wish, he immediately recited two verses:

5-6. I know that the birds' friendship is sincere,
The intelligent person must surely welcome it,
I give the bird whatever it wants,
You, wish to satisfy your wishes.

Hearing that, Vu Vuong recited the seventh verse to express his wish:

7. Swan, if you want to give grace,
Wish for the tree to gradually revive,
Rise to its old strength once again,
Fresh and delicious fruit grows all over the body.

Then Lord Sakka recited the eighth verse and bestowed this favor:

8. You look! The precious tree is full of fruit,
Suitable for the birds in this place,
Once again rising to its old strength,
The fruit is delicious, sweet, cool and fresh!

With these words, Sakka took off his goose guise, demonstrated miraculous powers with Queen Suja, and used his hand to scoop up water from the Ganges River and sprinkle it on the trunk of a fig tree. Immediately the tree sprouted luxuriant branches and leaves, full of fruits as sweet as honey, creating a magical scene like the exposed peak of Jade Mountain. Seeing this, Anh Vu was extremely happy and recited the ninth verse in praise of God Sakka:

9. Wishing that God, all the Angels,
May all enjoy a life full of blessings,
Happiness like a bird enjoying
When looking at the beautiful and splendid scene.

* * *

To illustrate this, verses derived from the Supreme wisdom of the Buddha are added at the end:

10. Just as the Vu Princess prayed,
Once again the tree gradually blossomed,
De Thich and the queen disappeared
Returning to the Paradise Garden of the 10 Angel Realms.

When the Dharma talk ended, the Master said:

- Thus, Bhikkhu, the wise men of the past, even though they were born as animals, abandoned craving. So why, now that you have been ordained into this supreme Dharma, do you still follow greedy habits?Go back and stay there.

And He gave this person a topic of meditation, then identified the previous incarnation:

- The Bhikkhu returned and through meditation attained Holy Fruition - "At that time Sakka was Anuruddha (Anuruddha) and the lord of the universe was Me".

Comment:

Less desire and contentment is one of the basic virtues of the Brahman life that the Buddha always encouraged monks to practice on the path to enlightenment and liberation. On the occasion of a Bhikkhu visiting the Buddha and presenting all his difficulties in a certain residence, the Buddha advised him to patiently endure the situation in a place full of kindness from good friends who had wholeheartedly served him before, even though later they had to suffer deprivation and hinder his practice because there was not enough food to make offerings as desired.

Then He told a Jataka story that proved His lack of desire when he was born as a blackbird. He kept all his affection for the fig tree that once fed the flock of birds. Now that the tree was damaged, He still did not want to leave it, even though there was only a little bit of rotten wood left, while the flock of birds had flown away to find food elsewhere.

Not only in ancient times, but when the Buddha was still alive, the Buddha still promoted the virtue of few desires and contentment and he once demonstrated that virtue to the extreme during his residence in Veranoja and this event was recorded in the Vinaya Pitaka. At that time, he was invited by a Brahmin in Veranoja to settle down in that place. But because of the bad harvest, he could not offer good food as planned. The Buddha patiently stayed there during the three-month retreat season and lived only on milled grain to show his gratitude to his good friend who was in trouble.

In the Dharma Inheritance Sutra (Middle Nikaya), the Buddha also taught the Bhikkhus to strive to become inheritors of the Dharma, not heirs of property, even though they have to endure difficult circumstances. And in many other sutras, the Buddha also advised his disciples to only stay in places that are convenient for personal practice even though they lack material resources, and to immediately stay away from places that are rich in material means but are not favorable for practicing to escape the world. And this is a teaching full of practical benefits for Buddhist disciples who want to practice His Holy Path in all times.

tieu_de: Story of the Filial Elephant Caring for His Mother
tom_tat: The Story of the Elephant Lovingly Nurturing His Mother (455. Formerly of Mati-Posaka) "Even if the king elephant had to go far away" This story was told by the Master while staying at Jetavana about a Bhikkhu whose mother had to be cared for. The circumstances of this story are similar to the Sàma story (number 540, volume VI).
noi_dung:
The story of an elephant taking care of his mother

(455. Precursor of Mãti-Posaka)

"Even if the king's elephant has to go far away"

This story was told by the Master while staying at Jetavana about a Bhikkhu whose mother
had to take care of.

The circumstances of this story are similar to the story of Sàma (number 540, volume VI).
On this occasion, the Master spoke to the Sangha. He said:

- Hey monks, don't be angry with this monk. Once upon a time, the sage, even when he was born from the belly of an animal, and was far away from his mother, refused to eat or drink anything for seven days, remaining thin and exhausted. Even though he was provided with royal food, he only replied: "Without my mother, I don't want to eat." However, when he saw his mother again, he refused to eat as before.

After saying that, he told a story from the past.

* * *

Once upon a time, when King Brahmadatta reigned in Ba La Nai, Bodhisattva was born as the Great Elephant King in the Snow Mountain region. The entire white elephant's body is very majestic, it is the lord of a herd of eighty thousand elephants surrounding him, but his mother is blind. He often gave the elephants delicious forest fruits to bring back to offer to their mother, but they did not bring anything back to offer to their mother, they ate it all. When he inquired and learned about it, he said:

- I want to leave the flock to raise my mother.

At that time, a lumberjack in Ba La Nai lost his way and could not find the way out, so he began to cry loudly. Hearing this sound, the Bodhisattva thought to himself: "That is a person in trouble. While I am here, it is not right that he should encounter disaster." So he approached him, but he ran away because he was so afraid; Seeing that, the elephant king told him: - Hey man, you don't need to be afraid of me, don't run away, tell me why you're crying as you walk?

- My lord, this coward has been lost for the past seven days.

The elephant lord replied:

- Don't be afraid anymore, and I will lead you to the path of the people.

Then he told the person to climb up and sit on his back and took him out of the forest, then he returned.

And that cruel man decided to go to the city to inform the king. So he marked the trees and hills, then headed towards Ba La Nai. At that time, the emperor's statue had just passed away. He gave the command with a drum beat.

- If anyone sees an elephant worthy of standing for the king to visit, please report it immediately.

Then that guy came to the king and said:

- Dear Lord, I saw a beautiful elephant, all white, a supreme object worthy of Your Majesty to sit on. The little god asked for directions. But please bring the mahouts along to catch the elephants.

The worker went with him and saw the Bodhisattva eating and drinking in a lake. When the Bodhisattva saw the woodsman, he thought: "This danger certainly does not come from anyone else, other than that person. But I am very strong, I can smash thousands of elephants in a moment of rage, I am strong enough to destroy an entire herd of elephants in battle of a kingdom. However, if I am dominated by anger, my merit will be damaged. Therefore today I will not be angry, even if a sword and spear pierce my skin." With this decision, he bowed his head and stood motionless.

The woodsman stepped into the lotus pond. When he saw the beauty of the ivory tip, he said:

- Hey, come here. Then, holding the trunk like a silver rope, he led the elephant back to Ba Na Nai city within seven days.

When Bodhisattva's mother saw that her son had not returned, she guessed that he must have been captured by the king's army.

- Now the trees still grow, but my children have gone far.

And she recited the following two verses:

1. Even if the royal elephant has to go far away,
The medicinal herb frankincense still grows,
Grass grass, oleander, and white lilies,
Green trumpets in hidden places still bloom.

2. The king's statue must go far away
Wealthy thanks to many high-ranking men,
Dressed in jewels and gold to ride on,
Majestic in defeating enemies wearing robes.

At that time, the elephant trainer, while still on the road, sent a petition to the king. The king immediately ordered the entire capital to be decorated splendidly. The elephant tamer led the Bodhisattva into a cage decorated with tassels and garlands and surrounded each with colorful curtains, then presented it to the king. The king brought out delicacies and told him to give them to the Bodhisattva, but he did not eat anything: "If it weren't for my mother, I wouldn't want to eat anything."

The king begged him to eat and recite the third verse:

3. Come on, take a bite, elephant,
Don't be sad, don't wither and become thin,
To serve the king, there are many tasks
that elephants will take on later.

Hearing that, the Bodhisattva recited the fourth verse:

4. No, on the top of Chien Do Gia mountain
Poor woman, her eyes are blind,
Stamped one foot on the root of an ancient tree
Because there is no king elephant, that is her son.
